author: Unreal Engine
description:
Watch this video for a look at the Unreal Engine 5 Next-Gen HMI Experience, revealed at CES 2026. 

Developed in technical collaboration with AMD and running on the Ryzen™ AI Embedded P100 Series, this project demonstrates the power of “driving every pixel” inside a digital cockpit from a single UE5 instance—including the instrument cluster, maps, mini map, control panel, and 3D backgrounds—on high-resolution displays running at 60 fps. 

Much more than a demo, this project is designed to be the gold standard for visual fidelity, performance, and interactivity in automotive HMI development.

To learn more about the capabilities of the Unreal Engine 5 Next-Gen HMI Experience, read our recap from CES 2026: https://www.unrealengine.com/en-US/news/unreal-engine-is-everywhere-at-ces-2026-from-hmis-to-simulation-and-beyond

author: Unreal Engine
description:
SECRET UE5 ANIMATION TIPS: Mastering the Tweener Tool (Push/Pull & Overshoot): Explore the various modes of the Tweener Tool used to quickly adjust keyframes and blend character poses. Contrast the default Blend Neighbor mode, which blends from the current pose, with the Tween mode, which snaps the pose immediately to the 50% midpoint between neighbors. 

Practice using Blend Ease to quickly create eased keyframes, Push Pull to amplify or de-amplify the pose's tension (and create overshoots), and Smooth Rough to smooth out or add jitter to animation data.

►Download the A-COM Animation Sample here: https://epic.gm/agora-animation-sample

title: Mastering the UE5 Tweener Tool: Push Pull & Overshoot Animation

author: Unreal Engine
description:
UE 5.6 CURVE EDITOR OVERHAUL: Lattice Tool & Smart Snap for Clean Animation: Master the redesigned Unreal Engine Curve Editor, including features introduced in Unreal Engine 5.6.

Learn to optimize your workspace using Normalized mode to maximize vertical screen space for selected curves or Stacked view for independent curve display. Discover powerful new editing tools like the Lattice tool for skewing or flipping curves and the Smart Snap feature (Ctrl+H) to cleanly reduce dense keyframe data to whole frames.
